finding.title: Add regression tests for GoalRepositoryImpl's not-found and delete-sync payload paths
finding.rule: EH-2 (typed exceptions surfaced correctly) / TQ-8 (every reachable error branch needs a red-first test)

evidence.quote:
if (existing == null) {
        throw ArgumentError('Goal not found: $goalId');

finding.why: (a) updateGoal throws ArgumentError when goalId doesn't exist (e.g. the goal was deleted from another device and the sync merge already removed the local row before this device's in-flight edit lands) — no test in this file ever calls updateGoal with a nonexistent id, so nothing pins whether it throws, what it throws, or that a future refactor doesn't silently swallow/change it. (b) The file's own 'sync payload completeness (R4-6)' group exists specifically because create/update once shipped without profile_id/id in the outbox payload — but that hardening was never extended to deleteGoal: _RecordingGoalSyncFacade.deleteGoal is a blind no-op with no payload recorder (unlike goalPayloads for pushGoal), and the sole 'deleteGoal removes the goal' test uses the sync-less `repo` instance, so _syncDeleteGoal's {firestore_id, curriculum_id} payload is completely unverified. A key rename or dropped field in _syncDeleteGoal would ship silently — the exact class of bug R4-6 was written to catch for create/update.
finding.recommendation: Add a test asserting updateGoal(goalId: <nonexistent>) throws ArgumentError; add a deletePayloads recorder to _RecordingGoalSyncFacade and a test asserting deleteGoal() pushes the expected firestore_id/curriculum_id payload, mirroring the existing R4-6 create/update tests.
acceptance_criteria: New red-first test fails against a deliberately-broken updateGoal (e.g. the null check removed) and passes against current code.
New deleteGoal-payload test fails if _syncDeleteGoal's field names are renamed or dropped, mirroring the existing R4-6 create/update tests.

finding.title: Split the four scheduler_engine test files that exceed AG-3's 400-line cap

evidence.quote: // Extra coverage for SchedulerEngine — weekly and rolling schedule types.
/// Unit tests for Story 26.3 (DNI-346) scheduler bug fixes.

finding.why: AG-3 caps hand-written Dart files (tests included, generated exempt) at 400 lines; these four all exceed it: scheduler_engine_test.dart 516, scheduler_engine_schedule_types_test.dart 507, scheduler_engine_self_paced_test.dart 431, scheduler_engine_dni346_test.dart 553 lines (wc -l, confirmed). Content quality in all four is otherwise good — distinct scenarios, hermetic hand-rolled fakes, strong exact-value assertions — the size comes from accretion across fix waves without ever re-splitting. Large files raise merge-conflict surface and make it harder for a contributor to find which of several hundred tests already covers a given branch of the 747-line scheduler_engine.dart they collectively exercise (itself already over AG-3, but that lib file is outside this batch).
finding.recommendation: Split by the group()s each file already has: e.g. scheduler_engine_dni346_test.dart's five 'Fix N' groups each become their own file; scheduler_engine_test.dart's legacy-pacing vs custom-order/priority-ranking groups split similarly.
acceptance_criteria: `wc -l` on every hand-written file under test/features/scheduler/ is <=400, matching the AG-3 [P]ending checker's intended threshold once implemented.

finding.title: Move overdue_from_elapsed_study_days_test.dart to mirror its domain/projection lib target
finding.why: The code under test is lib/features/scheduler/domain/projection/{projection,overdue_projection,overdue_schedule,overdue_types}.dart — pure Dart with zero Drift/repository dependency (the test file itself has no db/DAO setup at all, only elapsedStudyDays/selfPacedSchedule/project calls) — yet it lives at test/features/scheduler/data/repositories/. No test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/ directory exists at all (confirmed via find), so this is the projection module's only test and it's unmirrored. A future contributor searching test/.../domain/projection/ for existing coverage before adding a new projection test would find nothing and could re-create the exact duplication pattern flagged above for goal_entity/scheduler_content_repository/daily_task_generator.
finding.recommendation: Move the file to test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/overdue_from_elapsed_study_days_test.dart (create the directory); no import changes are needed since it already imports via the projection.dart barrel.
acceptance_criteria: File relocated; `flutter test test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/` runs and passes.

finding.title: Replace the hardcoded trackId:1 literal with the captured track id in two scheduler tests
finding.why: Both files insert a real curriculumTracks row and capture its autoincrement id into a `trackId` local specifically so downstream code can reference the real id — and both then ignore that variable and hardcode `trackId: 1` in the ScheduleConfig/generator.generate() calls that drive the assertions, while still correctly using the captured `trackId` variable a few lines away for the StageDefinitions/CompletionEvents inserts. It works today only because a fresh in-memory DB's first insert is always id 1 (verified: neither seedProfile nor seedProfileZero touch curriculumTracks). If either helper is ever extended to seed a track, or a second track is inserted earlier in a shared setUp, config.trackId/DailyTask.trackId would silently diverge from the row the stages/completions actually reference, and no assertion in either file would catch it since nothing currently checks task.trackId's value.
finding.recommendation: Replace the `trackId: 1` literals with the captured `trackId` variable in both files; add one assertion per file that a produced DailyTask.trackId equals the seeded track's real id, so the variable is load-bearing rather than decorative.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -n 'trackId: 1,'` in both files returns nothing after the fix.
At least one test per file asserts DailyTask.trackId against the captured trackId variable.

finding.title: Drop the hard-coded 500ms wall-clock assertion from scheduler_engine_performance_test.dart

evidence.quote:
final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
      final tasks = await engine.generateDailyTasks(config);

finding.why: This test asserts a hard wall-clock budget (elapsedMilliseconds < 500) for a 5,000-item/10,000-completion synchronous computation, running inside the same hermetic unit suite as every other file in this batch (no @Tags/exclusion). It passed on this run, but pass/fail now depends on host CPU speed and contention from parallel test-runner isolates/CI-runner noise, not on SchedulerEngine's correctness — a classic Nygard/Fowler 'erratic test.' A spurious failure on a busy CI runner produces a false-negative unrelated to the diff under review, and the natural response ('just rerun it') erodes trust in the suite over time.
finding.recommendation: Tag it out of the default hermetic run (e.g. `@Tags(['perf'])`, matching how the repo already tags story-acceptance suites) so it runs in a dedicated, less contention-sensitive job, or replace the absolute threshold with a much wider safety margin / relative-regression check.
acceptance_criteria: Test is excluded from the default `flutter test` sweep, or its threshold is widened enough (e.g. 5-10x measured baseline) to tolerate CI contention while still catching a genuine algorithmic regression (e.g. an accidental O(n^2) reintroduction).
